fullName: Coherent Surface Scattering Imaging beamline (APS-U feature beamline at 9-ID; stations 9-ID-D and 9-ID-GT 'Grand Tube')

status2026.detail: Operations of the old 9-ID (USAXS, Bionanoprobe) were suspended on 2022-08-01 and the old enclosures were removed by 2022-12-22 (r6, r7). The Grand Tube was unloaded in four sections in August 2023 and installed in Sep-Oct 2023 (r23, r41, r7). The user manual says 'Since first light in 2024-2, 9-ID operates with a single revolver undulator' (r9). That date must refer to the source/front end, because X-rays could not enter 9-ID-A before its shielding verification on 2024-12-18. Shielding verification: 9-ID-A and 9-ID-MH on 2024-12-18, 9-ID-D and 9-ID-GT (Grand Tube) on 2025-01-28..30 (r7, r6). Technical commissioning began 2025-02-03; 9-ID 'transitioned to full operations' on 2026-03-14; run 2026-2 (from 2026-05-27) gave 50% of beamtime through the Beamtime Allocation Committee and run 2026-3 (from 2026-09-09) gives 80% of beamtime to General User Proposals for GI-SAXS/WAXS/XPCS and CSSI (r6). The Beamline Directory lists 9-ID-D as 'Operational/Accepting General Users', on-site access (r5). Still incomplete vs the 2019 design: only the downstream undulator slot is filled (upstream empty, r9, r14); no liquid-surface diffractometer or multilayer monochromator appears in the as-built component lists (r8).

tagline: A 20-metre walk-in vacuum tube that turns X-ray 'glints' off flat surfaces into 3D nanoscale images and movies.
plainSummary: Many modern technologies live in layers thinner than a soap bubble: computer chips, solar-cell films, battery coatings, plastic electronics. Seeing what happens inside those layers is hard, because they sit on thick, opaque supports. CSSI solves this by skimming an extremely pure, laser-like X-ray beam across the surface at a fraction of a degree, like skipping a stone on a pond. The film scatters a tiny fraction of the X-rays into a grainy 'speckle' pattern, a fingerprint of every bump and buried edge. To read that fingerprint, the detector must be far away so each speckle spreads over many pixels: so the beamline ends in the Grand Tube, a 20-metre-long stainless-steel vacuum tube nearly 3 metres wide, inside which a camera with 18 million pixels rides on a carriage. Computers then work backwards from the speckles to a 3D picture. Watching how the speckles twinkle over time also reveals how films flow, wrinkle or self-organise, from thousandths of a second to many minutes. The upgraded APS makes this possible because it delivers roughly 100 times more coherent X-rays than before: the 'orderly' share of the beam rose from about 0.05% to several percent.
expertSummary: 9-ID is a single, non-canted ID beamline (revolver U21/U25, 2.35 m, downstream slot of a dual-inline straight; upstream slot empty) behind a windowless HHL front end. All beam-steering optics upstream of the KB deflect horizontally (the public sources do not state why; keeping vibrations out of the vertical plane is the usual reason): two horizontally deflecting mirrors (MR-1 flat, MR-2 bendable; Pt/Si/Cr stripes) and an LN2-cooled horizontally deflecting DCM in 9-ID-A, followed by a zoom focusing system: CRL-1 transfocator in the 9-ID-MH mini-hutch (~43 m), CRL-2 (~51 m) and a bendable KB pair (V then H; Pt-coated in the FDR; ~54 m, ~650 mm working distance, 0.5 um diffraction-limited target, 14-19 nrad angular stability; sample stability 55 nrad per SPIE 2025) in 9-ID-D. Tunable 6-25 keV; spots from ~0.5 to ~30 um. Station 9-ID-D hosts the CSSI solid-sample station (z = 54.992 m; vertical sample surface, horizontal scattering plane, 5-axis flexure nanopositioning with interferometric/capacitive metrology), a high-load hexapod for GI-XPCS, and the GIXS diffractometer migrated from 8-ID-E (z = 56.590 m; horizontal samples, in-air Pilatus 1M-F for GIWAXS). Downstream, the 9-ID-GT 'Grand Tube' (2.75 m x 20.5 m, 8 mm stainless steel, pink-beam-rated) carries an in-vacuum EIGER 16M and an MM-PAD on a 3-axis carriage at 2.9-21.8 m from the CSSI sample, giving speckle oversampling with 75-150 um pixels and q-space tiling. Techniques: CSSI (phase retrieval with DWBA/multislice/holographic forward models, rotation series), GI-XPCS (1 ms-1000 s), GISAXS/GIWAXS with operando environments.

whatAPSUEnables.plain: CSSI is a technique that only works with very 'orderly' (coherent) X-rays. The old APS beam was mostly disorderly: in a 2012 test at the APS it took a few hours to collect one usable pattern from a specially made, oversized gold test pattern. The new APS delivers about a hundred times more coherent X-rays, so useful patterns can be collected from realistic samples quickly enough to follow changes. For movies of speckle 'twinkling' the gain is even larger. For the same signal quality, the fastest measurable change scales with the square of the brightness, so in principle changes up to about 10,000 times faster become measurable. In practice the detector frame rate sets the limit, about a millisecond at 9-ID.
whatAPSUEnables.expert: The MBA lattice (41.5 pm natural emittance; zero-current ID source ~12-15 um x 3-8 um rms, r15) raises the coherent fraction at 10 keV from ~0.05% (pre-upgrade, sigma_x ~275 um) to ~3% (round-beam mode) or ~6% (flat-beam mode), i.e. ~50-130x, and the horizontal coherence length at 30 m from ~2 um to ~40-50 um (derived here from r15, single-electron photon terms for a 2.35 m device). Peak brilliance of the U21/U25 revolver is ~1-2e22 ph/s/mm2/mrad2/0.1%BW near 9-11 keV. That is 'two orders of magnitude' above the pre-upgrade Undulator A (r3); the 9-ID source slide shows ~1e20 for the old U33, i.e. ~100-200x (r9). The same slide's coherent-fraction curve (~6% at 10 keV, ~2% at 25 keV vs ~0.05% / ~0.015% for the old APS) matches the flat-beam derivation here. For XPCS, SNR = beta * I * sqrt(T tau N) grows linearly with intensity (brilliance), so at fixed SNR and total time the shortest accessible correlation time falls as 1/brilliance^2, ~1e4x shorter for ~100x (r9). In practice the detector frame rate (~1-2.5 ms) is the limit. Coherence-preserving horizontal-deflection optics, nano-focusing (to ~0.5 um) and a 20 m in-vacuum flight path with 75-150 um-pixel detectors let the speckle be oversampled even at 25 keV, while 3D detector translation extends q-coverage to nm-scale resolution.
quantitative: Coherent fraction at 10 keV: ~0.05% pre-upgrade (sigma_x 275 um, sigma_y 10 um) vs ~2.6% (round mode) / ~6% (flat mode) for the 2.35 m revolver on APS-U (derived here from r15 source parameters; formula lambda/4pi per plane)
Horizontal coherence length at 30 m, 10 keV: ~2 um pre-upgrade vs ~48 um (round) / ~41 um (flat) on APS-U; vertical ~58 um vs ~70-160 um (derived, xi = lambda z / (2 pi Sigma); r15)

Peak brilliance of the U21/U25 revolver >1e22 ph/s/mrad2/mm2/0.1%BW at 10 keV, 'two orders of magnitude higher than the current Undulator A' (r3; also source-characteristics slide r9); the 9-ID slide shows U21 1st harmonic ~2e22 near 10-11 keV vs ~1.1e20 peak for the old APS U33 (r9)
Pre-upgrade APS delivered 0.01%-0.1% coherent photons over the hard X-ray range (r3)
2012 CSSI demonstration at 8-ID-E: ~1e9 coherent ph/s, 7.35 keV, sample-detector 0.7 m, a few hours per pattern, max 3000 counts; resolutions 2.6 um x 22 nm x 2.7 nm (r3, r24)

Design flux at 9-ID with KB focusing at 8.8 keV: 9.2e13 ph/s/0.1%BW into 0.75 x 0.42 um (3x2 coherent modes); CRL-2: 9.4e13 into 3.5 x 1.7 um; CRL-1 full beam: 3.4e14 into 29 x 16 um (FDR Table 4.58, r1). Directory quotes ~1.2e13 ph/s for the KB mode (r5)

XPCS: at fixed SNR the shortest accessible time scales as 1/brilliance^2 (the r9 slide words it 'scales as (Brilliance)^2', meaning the improvement factor) -> ~1e4 shorter for a ~100x brilliance gain; GI-XPCS at 9-ID targets 1e-3 to 1e3 s (r5, r19)
Sample-to-detector distance 2.9-21.8 m in vacuum (r4) vs 0.7 m in the 2012 demonstration (r3)
9-ID source slide (r9): coherent fraction ~6% at 10 keV and ~2% at 25 keV (APS-U, U25/U21) vs ~5e-4 and ~1.4e-4 (APS, U33), i.e. ~100-150x (read from plot)

PDR (2017) promised 'two to three orders of magnitude increase in coherent flux'; it assumed a 4.8 m undulator length. As built there is one 2.35 m device, so ~100-200x is the realistic gain (r3, r9, r14)

techniques.name: Coherent Surface Scattering Imaging
techniques.plain: A lens-free way of taking 3D pictures of tiny structures sitting on a surface. The X-ray beam grazes the surface; the scattered light forms a speckle pattern that a computer turns back into an image, like reconstructing an object from the sparkle it makes.
techniques.expert: Coherent diffractive imaging in grazing-incidence reflection geometry near the critical angle (alpha_i ~0.1-1 deg). Ewald-sphere intersection gives sensitivity to qz; oversampled speckle (lambda D / (p d) >= 2) recorded without a beamstop on a high-dynamic-range detector. Reconstruction must handle dynamical (multibeam) scattering: DWBA with four reflection/transmission paths, finite-element DWBA, multislice forward models with autodiff, and nonuniform-FFT iterative phasing of rotation series (in-plane phi rotation of a few degrees fills the poorly resolved beam-direction axis). 2012 demo (8-ID-E, 7.35 keV, CCD at 0.7 m): 2.6 um x 22 nm x 2.7 nm resolution (along-beam x in-plane x surface-normal). Later work with more flux and better detectors (APS 8-ID, PETRA III P10) pushed in-plane resolution below 5 nm, and ptychographic CSSI has reconstructed extended patterns (r3, r24, r29, r25, r27, r28).

techniques.name: Grazing-Incidence X-ray Photon Correlation Spectroscopy
techniques.plain: Instead of a still picture, watch how the speckle pattern twinkles. Fast twinkling means the surface is moving fast. This measures how thin films flow, roughen or rearrange without touching them.
techniques.expert: Intensity autocorrelation g2(q,tau) = <I(t)I(t+tau)>/<I>^2 of the speckle in GISAXS geometry, evanescent-wave depth selection below/above alpha_c; relaxation rates Gamma(q) distinguish diffusion (q^2), overdamped capillary waves (Gamma = gamma q/(2 eta) for thick films) and ballistic/jamming dynamics (q^1). At 9-ID: in-vacuum EIGER 16M at 3-20 m, 1 ms-1000 s, high-load hexapod sample stage; GPU correlation with boost-corr in automated DM workflows (r5, r19, r40).

techniques.name: Grazing-Incidence Small-Angle X-ray Scattering
techniques.plain: Measures the average size, spacing and shape of nanoscale features (pores, grains, stripes) across a whole film.
techniques.expert: Ensemble-averaged nanostructure (1-100s nm) of supported films via DWBA analysis (GIXSGUI, GIXS-U), with in situ thermal/solvent-vapour annealing, spin-coating and deposition; EIGER 16M in the Grand Tube provides long camera lengths (r5, r38, r40).

techniques.name: Grazing-Incidence Wide-Angle X-ray Scattering
techniques.plain: Shows how molecules or atoms are stacked and which way crystals point in a thin film, for example in solar cells or plastic electronics.
techniques.expert: Molecular/crystal packing and texture of thin films via an in-air Pilatus 1M-F (135 fps) on the WAXS detector motion system 9ID-BI-7 next to the GIXS diffractometer; operando electrochemistry, Linkam HFSX350-GI stage (-180..300 C per directory), UR3e sample robot (r5, r8).

techniques.name: Grazing-incidence multibeam X-ray holography (Lloyd's-mirror surface holography)
techniques.plain: The flat substrate acts as a mirror: light scattered by the sample interferes with its own reflection, creating a hologram that encodes the height of features, sometimes from a single snapshot.
techniques.expert: Interference between the scattered wave from a 3D surface pattern and its substrate-reflected copy near the horizon (alpha_f < ~0.3 deg) gives dark-field, low-noise holographic fringes with period ~2 pi/(2d) in qz for a scatterer at height d; analysed with FE-DWBA (more than 5 million cells) and a first-principles holographic propagation model to recover 3D form factors at nm/sub-nm resolution from a single view (r25, r26).

scienceCases.title: Seeing buried nanocircuits in 3D without cutting the chip
scienceCases.plain: Chip makers need to check the exact shape and height of tiny wires and layers, but slicing a chip to look inside destroys it. CSSI reads the 3D shape from X-rays bouncing off the surface, so the wafer stays intact.
scienceCases.expert: Substrate-supported, non-periodic patterns cannot be measured in transmission CDI or ptychography without thinning. CSSI and reflective holography give critical-dimension (CD) and height metrology of planar patterns on thick substrates; the 2012 proof of principle reconstructed a lithographic Au 'Argonne' pattern with 22 nm in-plane and ~2.7 nm normal resolution, and later APS/P10 data reached better than 5 nm in-plane (r29). The 2023 first-experiments workshop included a NIST talk, 'Metrology for Semiconductor Industry' (R. J. Kline) (r37).

scienceCases.title: 3D shape from a single snapshot: an X-ray Lloyd's mirror
scienceCases.plain: A famous 19th-century optics trick uses a mirror to make light interfere with its own reflection. At grazing angles the silicon substrate plays the mirror, and the resulting hologram reveals the height of a pattern from just one image.
scienceCases.expert: Chu et al. (2023) showed that multibeam scattering near total external reflection makes a single grazing-incidence view sensitive to 3D structure; FE-DWBA (more than 5 million cells) reproduces the data and a first-principles holographic model recovers stacked Au-bar thicknesses with nm/sub-nm precision (single Au bar at PETRA III P10: 8.0 keV, 1.7 x 3.5 um CRL focus, EIGER X 4M at 5.0 m, incidence 0.2-0.8 deg, 0.5-1e11 coherent ph/s; stacked bars at APS 8-ID-I: 7.35 keV, 2.2 x 2.5 um, Lambda 2M at 3.95 m, ~5e9 coherent ph/s, incidence 0.6 deg). This single-view mode is aimed at irreversible, in situ/operando processes at 9-ID.

scienceCases.title: Teaching computers to invert surface speckle (physics-informed reconstruction)
scienceCases.plain: Ordinary 'undo the Fourier transform' tricks fail near a mirror-like surface. New algorithms simulate the X-rays slice by slice and adjust a 3D model until the simulated speckle matches the measurement.
scienceCases.expert: Multislice forward model with PyTorch autodiff reconstructs elongated 3D patterns from single CSSI frames (8-ID prototype, 7.36 keV, ~2x2 um beam, flux 5e9 ph/s; simulations assume 100x more flux as at APS-U); a 2026 nonuniform-FFT iterative phasing framework derives sampling requirements and reconstructs isolated 3D objects from rotation series at as few as one or two incident angles.

scienceCases.title: Plastic electronics that breathe while they work
scienceCases.plain: Soft 'mixed conductor' polymers used in bio-sensors swell and shrink as ions flow in and out. Watching how grazing X-ray speckles flicker while the device is switched on and off shows the material's inner structure straining and slowly rearranging.
scienceCases.expert: Operando grazing-incidence XPCS of an acid-treated PEDOT:PSS film in an electrochemical 'cone cell' (RbBr or NaCl electrolyte) was measured at pre-upgrade APS 8-ID-I: 10.92 keV, 2 x 20 um beam, 10 Hz frames. Speckle dynamics tracked internal strain and mesoscale reorganisation during doping and de-doping, revealing structural hysteresis and a slow non-equilibrium process on re-doping (Wu et al., Nat. Mater. 2024, with 9-ID staff co-authors Strzalka, Narayanan and Zhang; complementary operando GIWAXS came from earlier work). At 9-ID the same studies combine GIWAXS on the former 8-ID-E instrument with GI-XPCS on the coherent APS-U beam over 1e-3 to 1e3 s.

scienceCases.title: Watching solar-cell films crystallise as they are spun
scienceCases.plain: Perovskite solar films form in seconds as a liquid is spun on a disc. X-rays show which chemical route the crystals take, and how to steer them to a stable, efficient film.
scienceCases.expert: In situ GIWAXS during spin coating of mixed 2D/3D halide perovskites revealed competing 'solvate' and 'orientation' formation mechanisms set by the precursor stoichiometry (Hoffman et al., Chem 2022; measured during 5-min spin-coating runs at APS 8-ID-E, the GIXS instrument that has since moved to 9-ID, per the APS highlight). '3D morphology of photovoltaic thin films' is one of the six prime CSSI research areas in the FDR; 9-ID supports spin coating, thermal and solvent-vapour annealing, and user solar simulators.

scienceCases.title: How thin films flow, roughen and self-organise
scienceCases.plain: Even a solid-looking plastic film has a restless surface with tiny waves. Speckle 'twinkling' measures how fast those waves relax, and how patterns grow when films are made or etched.
scienceCases.expert: GI-XPCS of ultrathin molten polystyrene films showed that the capillary-wave model must include a shear modulus (viscoelastic effects) (Jiang et al., PRL 2007), and coherent GISAXS follows self-organised ion-beam nanopatterning and thin-film growth (e.g. de Gennes narrowing, Myint et al., PRL 2021, measured at NSLS-II CHX). FDR science drivers include self-assembly at surfaces/interfaces, capillary instability in confined geometry and GI-XPCS of interfacial dynamics.

scienceCases.title: At-wavelength metrology of coherence-preserving X-ray mirrors
scienceCases.plain: Super-smooth X-ray mirrors must be flat to a fraction of a nanometre. CSSI can test them with the very X-rays they will reflect.
scienceCases.expert: Listed as a CSSI prime research area (FDR 4-8.1/4-8.6.1); the KB mirrors themselves need <0.3 nm (H) and <0.2 nm (V) rms figure error to keep focal broadening below 3%. 9-ID-D also carries a compact wavefront sensor (9ID-BD-6, APS Optics design) downstream of the CSSI station.

insertionDevices.name: Revolver undulator APS21R25#5 - U21 array (APS21#10)
insertionDevices.type: planar hybrid permanent-magnet revolver undulator (two magnet arrays on a rotating carriage)
insertionDevices.notes: 112 periods (length derived 112 x 21 mm = 2.35 m; slide says 2.3 m); device min gap 8.5 mm, admin min 8.72 mm, user min 9.0 mm; Keff 1.38 / E1 8.34 keV at 8.5 mm; Ptot 5.4 kW, Pdens 216 kW/mrad2 at 200 mA. Used for the high-flux 8.8 keV fundamental and its 3rd harmonic (26.4 keV) in the FDR design. Installed in the DOWNSTREAM slot (FDR: centre ~1.25 m downstream of the straight-section centre). The 9-ID source slide calls it a 'Tandem revolver undulator - 2.3 m long (21 and 25 mm periods)' with 'continuous tunability over 8-25 keV' (r9). ID table footnote: effective periods = N - 2 (r14). Estimated E1 at the 9.0 mm user minimum gap is ~8.9-9.0 keV, so the FDR's 8.8 keV U21 fundamental (K = 1.305) is just below reach on the U21 fundamental; the U25 array covers it.

source.canting: None. 9-ID is a dual-inline (non-canted) straight with a single device installed downstream; beam leaves along the straight axis.
source.frontEnd: APS-U High Heat Load Front End (HHLFE; limits 21 kW total, 590 kW/mrad2): permanent-magnet clearing magnet, LPPS, storage-ring valve, burn-through fixed mask BTFM1, FM2, collimator, GRID XBPM1, FM3, photon shutter PS2 with intensity monitor IM1, safety shutters SS1/SS2, wall collimator through the ratchet wall, then on the exit table in 9-ID-A: exit mask (2 x 2 mm, with XBPM2) at 25.4 m and tungsten exit collimator (5 x 5 mm) at 26.1 m. 9-ID uses the windowless exit with a built-in differential pump (r2 Table 3.1, Sec. 3-2.1; r1 4-8.3). FDR design power through the 2 x 2 mm mask: 2.10 kW for U21 with two devices (K 1.305), 0.812 kW for U25 (K 1.939) (r1 Table 4.56).
source.sourceSizeAndDivergence: Electron beam at an ID straight (r15, Aug 2024; values are for ZERO current; intrabeam scattering at 200 mA enlarges them somewhat): round-beam mode sigma_x = 12.3 um, sigma_y = 8.26 um, sigma_x' = 2.34 urad, sigma_y' = 3.47 urad (28.7 pm each plane); flat-beam mode (kappa = 0.1) 14.5 / 3.08 um and 2.75 / 1.29 urad. Single-electron photon terms for L = 2.35 m (derived, sigma_r = sqrt(2 lambda L)/4pi, sigma_r' = sqrt(lambda/2L)): 1.9 um / 5.1 urad at 10 keV, 1.2 um / 3.2 urad at 25 keV - the photon divergence dominates, so the photon source is ~12.5 x 8.5 um rms and ~5.6 x 6.2 urad rms at 10 keV (round mode). PDR quoted APS-U ranges sigma_x 5-30 um, sigma_y 2-14 um vs 275 / 10 um pre-upgrade (r3 Table 6.18).

branches.name: 9-ID single line (pink or monochromatic)
branches.description: One beam path; no canting or branching. In monochromatic mode the HDCM displaces the beam horizontally: at 42.38 m the mono beam runs ~10 mm outboard of the pink-beam path (XBPM drawing, r10), and masks in 9-ID-A/MH (dual-aperture PM-5, pink beamstop BS-2) handle both paths. Three sample positions share the line inside 9-ID-D: CSSI solid-sample station (54.992 m), hexapod for GI-XPCS (~55.9 m) and GIXS diffractometer (56.590 m); all share the Grand Tube detectors downstream.

components.name: Upstream undulator slot (empty)
components.distanceNote: approx: mirror image of the downstream device position (+1.25 m, FDR Table 4.56); not given explicitly
components.plain: This half of the straight section is empty for now: a second undulator could be added later to make the beam even brighter.
components.expert: FDR baseline placed a planar U21 here (dual-inline straight with phase shifter/corrector between devices, FDR Table 3.13); the 2026 ID table lists no device in S09 US and the 9-ID manual says the slot can host a second undulator in the future.

components.name: Revolver undulator U21/U25 (APS21R25#5)
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.56: revolver centre 1.25 m downstream of the centre of the straight section (distance convention: from straight-section centre)
components.plain: Two rows of strong magnets above and below the electron beam make the electrons wiggle and emit an intense, narrow X-ray beam. The magnet rows can be swapped by rotating the device ('revolver') to pick a 21 mm or 25 mm magnetic period, which changes the colours (energies) it emits best.
components.expert: Hybrid PM revolver: U21 array (112 periods, Keff 1.38, E1 8.34 keV at 8.5 mm; 5.4 kW, 216 kW/mrad2) and U25 array (94 periods, Keff 1.99, E1 4.58 keV; 8.1 kW, 225 kW/mrad2), user min gap 9.0 mm. 1st and 3rd harmonics cover 6-25 keV; brilliance ~1e22 near 10 keV. Only device in the straight since first light (run 2024-2).

components.name: High-heat-load front end (in tunnel)
components.distanceNote: approx: front end occupies roughly 14-23 m inside the tunnel; 19.4 m is the documented XBPM1/upstream-mask position for APS-U front ends (FDR Table 3.9, CUFE) - HHLFE element positions for 9-ID are not published
components.plain: A chain of water-cooled blocks, shutters and beam monitors inside the shielding that tames the multi-kilowatt X-ray beam and can stop it instantly for safety.
components.expert: HHLFE (21 kW, 590 kW/mrad2 limits): clearing magnet, LPPS, SRV, BTFM1, FM2, collimator, GRID XBPM1, FM3, PS2/IM1, safety shutters SS1/SS2, wall collimator, FEV. Windowless configuration with built-in differential pumping for 9-ID.

components.name: Shield (ratchet) wall with wall collimator
components.distanceNote: approx: ~22.1-23.6 m by analogy with the 28-ID ray-trace plan used in the CHEX dossier; not documented for 9-ID
components.plain: The thick concrete wall between the accelerator tunnel and the experiment hall; the X-rays pass through a small hole.
components.expert: Front-end wall collimator sits in the ratchet-wall penetration; FDR Fig. 4.51 shows 9-ID-A starting at ~23.5-24 m.

components.name: Front-end exit mask (2 x 2 mm) with XBPM2
components.distanceNote: exact: FDR Table 4.57
components.plain: A water-cooled metal block with a 2 mm square hole that trims the beam to its useful core.
components.expert: Standard HHL exit mask, 2 (H) x 2 (V) mm, integrated XBPM2; differential pump instead of a Be window (windowless exit).

components.name: Front-end exit collimator
components.distanceNote: exact: FDR Table 4.57
components.plain: A tungsten block that stops stray high-energy radiation (bremsstrahlung) from following the X-ray beam.
components.expert: Tungsten exit collimator, 5 x 5 mm aperture (narrowed for small-offset monochromators, FDR 3-2.1.1).

components.name: Slits 9ID-SL-1
components.distanceNote: exact per FDR Table 4.57 (HHL white-beam slits w/ tungsten edge inserts); as-built label 'Slits, PB 9ID-SL-1'
components.plain: Four movable jaws that cut the beam to the size the experiment needs.
components.expert: High-heat-load white/pink-beam slits with W edges defining the mirror acceptance (~1 x 1 mm, FDR M1 acceptance 0.96 x 1.0 mm2).

components.name: Mirror 9ID-MR-1 (horizontal, flat)
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (r8, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: A super-smooth mirror hit at a glancing angle. It bounces the useful X-rays sideways and lets unwanted high-energy X-rays and much of the heat pass by, while keeping the beam's 'orderliness' intact.
components.expert: First optic; flat, horizontally deflecting, water-cooled (FDR: notched substrate to cut thermal bump by ~10x). As-built coating stripes selected by vertical translation: Pt, Si ('Si stripe for 8 keV'), Cr ('Cr for 11 keV') plus a fourth (manual: 4 stripes). FDR design: 2.4 mrad, Si/Pd/Pt; 474 W incident, 311 W absorbed, 0.82 W/mm2 at 8.8 keV (two-device source).

components.name: Secondary collimator 9ID-SC-1
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (r8, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m (FDR 29.1 m)
components.plain: A heavy-metal block that catches stray radiation scattered by the mirror.
components.expert: Bremsstrahlung/secondary collimator downstream of MR-1.

components.name: Diagnostic flag 9ID-BD-1 (WB/PB)
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (r8, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m (FDR 29.5 m)
components.plain: A glowing screen that can be dropped into the beam so a camera can see where the X-rays are.
components.expert: Diamond screen imaged by camera, 16.13 um/pixel (calibrated 2024-11-23); shows direct beam when MR-1 is retracted.

components.name: Photon mask / white-beam stop 9ID-PM-1
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (r8, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: A cooled block that absorbs the part of the beam the mirror did not reflect.
components.expert: Manual: 'Photon Mask, WB Stop, 9ID-PM-1' - absorbs the unreflected white beam passing MR-1 (the FDR placed its WB stop 9ID-PM-1 at 33.8 m, after the mono). The as-built layout labels it 'Photon Mask, PB, 9ID-PM-1'; the manual list calls it 'Photon Mask, WB Stop, 9ID-PM-1' (r8).

components.name: Movable photon mask 9ID-PM-2 ('DAMM')
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (r8, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: A movable mask that can be positioned to block or pass selected parts of the beam.
components.expert: Movable pink-beam photon mask labelled 'DAMM' in the as-built layout (manual lists a movable pinhole mask); acronym expansion not documented. The shielding analysis assumed a pinhole-defined source plus two mirrors (r20). The manual component list (ELOG 897) writes it as 'Pinhole Mask, Moveable, 9ID-PM-1', an evident numbering slip. The layout drawing labels it 'DAMM: Photon Mask, movable, PB, 9ID-PM-2'.

components.name: Secondary collimator 9ID-SC-2
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (r8, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: Another radiation-catching block.
components.expert: Secondary collimator ahead of MR-2.

components.name: Mirror 9ID-MR-2 (horizontal, bendable)
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (r8, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: A second glancing mirror that bounces the beam back parallel to its original direction. It can be gently bent to adjust how the beam converges.
components.expert: Not in the FDR (one mirror). Horizontally deflecting bender with the same 4-stripe layout as MR-1 (operated on Cr in the logged configuration). The two-mirror geometry gives extra harmonic rejection and keeps the line-of-sight blocked. It matches the assumption of the 2020 shielding design study for the pink-beam-rated Grand Tube: pinhole-defined source and two mirrors at >= 3.0 mrad (r20). Whether the as-built angles meet 3.0 mrad is not published.

components.name: Photon mask 9ID-PM-3
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (r8, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: Absorbs stray beam after the second mirror.
components.expert: Pink-beam photon mask.

components.name: Diagnostic flag 9ID-BD-2
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (r8, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: A camera screen to check the beam after the mirrors.
components.expert: Diamond screen, WB/PB flag.

components.name: Photon mask 9ID-PM-4
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (r8, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: Another protective mask.
components.expert: Pink-beam photon mask upstream of the monochromator.

components.name: Bremsstrahlung collimator 9ID-BC-1
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (r8, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m (listed in the manual between PM-4 and SL-2; FDR 34.2 m)
components.plain: A heavy collimator against high-energy stray radiation.
components.expert: Bremsstrahlung collimator.

components.name: Pink-beam slits 9ID-SL-2
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (r8, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m (FDR 29.9 m: moved downstream because a second mirror was added)
components.plain: Slits that trim the beam before the monochromator.
components.expert: H+V pink-beam slits.

components.name: Horizontal double-crystal monochromator 9ID-MN-1 (HDCM)
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (r8, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m (FDR 30.65 m)
components.plain: Two perfect silicon crystals pick out a single X-ray colour (energy) from the rainbow. They bounce the beam sideways rather than upward, so tiny wobbles of the crystals nudge the beam sideways instead of up and down. The single-colour beam comes out parallel to the original path, about 1 cm to the side.
components.expert: Horizontally deflecting DCM (APS seminar abstract, r19); LN2 cooling and fixed exit per FDR. FDR: Si(111) pseudo channel-cut, 13.0 deg at 8.8 keV, 163 W absorbed, footprint 4.65 x 1.08 mm. Contains flag 'Flag3 9ID-BD-3' (10 mm diamond region inboard + CdWO4 region outboard, viewed at 45 deg, 20.833 um/px; ELOG 906 attachment). The same tag 9ID-BD-3 is also used for XBPM-1 in 9-ID-MH (ELOG 898/909), so the manual has a naming clash. Mono beam exits ~10 mm outboard of the pink path (XBPM drawing at 42.38 m); FDR design had a ~2 mm offset. Vendor appears to be IDT ('IDT Mono', manual).

components.name: Dual-aperture photon mask 9ID-PM-5
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (r8, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: A mask with two holes: one for the 'pink' beam path and one for the single-colour beam path.
components.expert: Dual-aperture pink-beam mask passing both pink and mono beam positions.

components.name: Shielded transport 9-ID-A to 9-ID-MH
components.distanceNote: approx: between FOE wall (~36.9 m, FDR Fig. 4.51) and the mini-hutch (~41.5 m)
components.plain: A shielded vacuum pipe carrying the beam between enclosures.
components.expert: Shielded transport with support stands (~2 m spacing in FDR Fig. 4.51).

components.name: Pink beamstop 9ID-BS-2 (with gate valve GV-5)
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-MH layout and component list (r8, ELOG 898), anchored to the surveyed XBPM 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m (r10)
components.plain: A block that stops the full-spectrum ('pink') beam whenever only the single-colour beam, running about 1 cm to the side, is wanted downstream.
components.expert: Pink-beam stop at the upstream end of the mini-hutch; the mono beam passes ~10 mm outboard.

components.name: X-ray beam position monitor 9ID-BD-3 (XBPM-1)
components.distanceNote: exact: 42.380 m on the XBPM drawing; survey 2024-12-03 gave Z = 42.4186 m (r10)
components.plain: A sensor that tells, many times per second, exactly where the beam is, so drifts can be corrected.
components.expert: Sydor XBPM (SI-103770), +/-13 mm X, +/-5 mm Y travel; centred on the midplane between pink and mono beams (10 mm apart); 22 mm bypass aperture. Note: the 9-ID-A layout and ELOG 906 also call the mono flag 'Flag3 9ID-BD-3', so the BD-3 tag appears twice in the manual.

components.name: Pink-beam slits 9ID-SL-3
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-MH layout and component list (r8, ELOG 898), anchored to the surveyed XBPM 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m (r10)
components.plain: Slits that select the most coherent central part of the beam.
components.expert: Pink-beam slits (same mechanics as SL-4/SL-5).

components.name: Photon shutter 9ID-PH-1
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-MH layout and component list (r8, ELOG 898), anchored to the surveyed XBPM 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m (r10)
components.plain: A safety shutter that blocks the beam so people can enter the experiment station.
components.expert: Photon shutter (as-built label 'Photon Shutter, 9ID-PH-1'), upstream of CRL-1 in the mini-hutch. Its safety role (protecting entry to 9-ID-D) is inferred from the name and position, not documented.

components.name: Transfocator CRL-1 (9ID-RL-1)
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-MH layout and component list (r8, ELOG 898), anchored to the surveyed XBPM 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m (r10); FDR placed CRL-1 at 32.4 m in the FOE
components.plain: A stack of tiny curved beryllium lenses that can be slid in or out to focus the X-rays loosely onto the sample, the first stage of a 'zoom lens'.
components.expert: 9 cassettes, all 2D parabolic: N = 1,1,1,1,1,1,2,4,8 with R = 2000,1000,500,300,200,100,100,100,100 um (9ID CRL final design review). Provides the larger GIXS/GI-XPCS spots and prefocus for the zoom with CRL-2/KB. FDR version had 12 stacks incl. 1D lenses.

components.name: Diagnostic flag 9ID-BD-4
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-MH layout and component list (r8, ELOG 898), anchored to the surveyed XBPM 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m (r10)
components.plain: A screen and camera to check the focused beam.
components.expert: PB/MB flag.

components.name: Shutter 9ID-SH-1
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-MH layout and component list (r8, ELOG 898), anchored to the surveyed XBPM 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m (r10) (FDR: pink shutter at 35.5 m)
components.plain: Another beam shutter at the exit of the mini-hutch.
components.expert: Station shutter (FDR 'Shutter, Pink, 9ID-SH-1').

components.name: Fast shutter 9ID-BI-8
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-D layout and component list (r8, ELOG 895), anchored to XBPM 9ID-BD-5 at 53.43 m (r10) and the CSSI station at 54.992 m (r8, ELOG 916) (FDR slits at 47.7 m)
components.plain: A quick shutter that opens only while the detector is recording, to avoid damaging delicate films.
components.expert: Fast experimental shutter on the upstream optical table, synchronised with detector exposures (softGlue timing).

components.name: Attenuator 9ID-AT-1
components.distanceNote: approx: FDR filters at 48.2 m; as-built on the same table as the fast shutter (r8)
components.plain: Thin metal foils that dim the beam when it is too strong for the sample or detector.
components.expert: Pink/mono-beam filter attenuator.

components.name: Pink-beam slits 9ID-SL-4
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-D layout and component list (r8, ELOG 895), anchored to XBPM 9ID-BD-5 at 53.43 m (r10) and the CSSI station at 54.992 m (r8, ELOG 916)
components.plain: Slits that clean up the beam before the second lens set.
components.expert: Coherence-defining/cleanup slits upstream of CRL-2 (PDR planned coherence slits ~50 m: 2x vertical, 3x horizontal coherence length).

components.name: Transfocator CRL-2 (9ID-RL-2)
components.distanceNote: approx: FDR Table 4.57 value; as-built order SL-4 -> RL-2 -> SL-5 (r8)
components.plain: The second, stronger set of X-ray lenses, focusing the beam to a few micrometres for coherent experiments.
components.expert: 10 cassettes, all 2D: N = 1,1,1,1,1,1,2,4,8,16, R = 2000-100 um (cassettes 9 and 10 annotated as swapped). FDR: 3.5 x 1.7 um (H x V) at 8.8 keV with a 3x2-mode coherent aperture, 9.4e13 ph/s/0.1%BW.

components.name: Pink-beam slits 9ID-SL-5
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-D layout and component list (r8, ELOG 895), anchored to XBPM 9ID-BD-5 at 53.43 m (r10) and the CSSI station at 54.992 m (r8, ELOG 916)
components.plain: Final slits before the focusing mirrors.
components.expert: Pink-beam slits.

components.name: X-ray beam position monitor 9ID-BD-5 (XBPM-2)
components.distanceNote: exact: 53.432 m on the XBPM drawing; survey 2024-12-03 gave Z = 53.3988 m (r10)
components.plain: A second beam-position sensor just before the focusing mirrors.
components.expert: Sydor XBPM, same assembly as BD-3.

components.name: Kirkpatrick-Baez mirror pair 9ID-MR-3
components.distanceNote: approx: FDR has V-KB 1.0 m and H-KB 0.8 m upstream of the 55 m sample (54.0/54.2 m); SPIE 2025 quotes a ~650 mm working distance to the CSSI sample at 54.992 m
components.plain: Two curved mirrors at right angles, one squeezing the beam vertically and one horizontally, focus it to about half a micrometre, 200 times thinner than a hair.
components.expert: Two bendable flat mirrors, V upstream of H (FDR: Pt coating, 2.5 mrad; as-built coating and angles not published), piezo-lever weak-link flexure benders, flexure alignment stages with a 4-interferometer metrology frame in UHV chambers on granite air-bearing stages. Targets: 500 nm diffraction-limited focus at ~650 mm WD; angular stability 19 nrad (H) / 14 nrad (V); figure error <0.3 nm (H) / <0.2 nm (V) rms. FDR spots: 0.75 x 0.42 um at 8.8 keV, 0.66 x 0.35 um at 26.4 keV. Manual geometry: hexapod centre is 1.818 m from KB-V and 1.552 m from KB-H, so the two mirrors are ~0.27 m apart (r8, ELOG 916). The KB and the CSSI sample station sit on one shared granite table (r17).

components.name: Window 9ID-WN-1 (Be or SiN)
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-D layout and component list (r8, ELOG 895), anchored to XBPM 9ID-BD-5 at 53.43 m (r10) and the CSSI station at 54.992 m (r8, ELOG 916)
components.plain: A paper-thin window separating the ultra-clean vacuum of the mirrors from the sample chamber.
components.expert: Be or SiN window between KB (UHV) and the CSSI sample chamber (high vacuum).

components.name: CSSI solid sample station 9ID-BI-2
components.distanceNote: exact: 'CSSI-SSS: 54992' mm (r8, ELOG 916)
components.plain: The heart of CSSI: a vacuum chamber where the sample stands on its edge and is tilted to a tiny grazing angle with nanometre precision, then turned a few degrees to view it from different directions.
components.expert: High-vacuum sample chamber; vertical sample surface reflecting in the horizontal plane. 5 DOF (3 linear + pitch about vertical axis + yaw about surface normal) with custom weak-link flexure stages (cm travel, nm MIM; piezo 1 mm stage; pitch correction <1 deg, tens-of-nrad MIM), three metrology frames (capacitive + laser interferometers; nm linear, 10s nrad angular). Requirement: 50 nrad sample angular stability (MEDSI 2020) / 55 nrad (SPIE 2025). The KB and the sample station share one granite table to cut floor noise and relative motion. High-precision commercial rotation stages give pitch (vertical axis) and yaw (horizontal axis). Three metrology frames: two measure parasitic motion of the rotation stages, one measures the flexure stages. Designed, assembled and installed at 9-ID (SPIE 2025, r17).

components.name: Wavefront sensor 9ID-BD-6
components.distanceNote: approx (+/- ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-D layout and component list (r8, ELOG 895), anchored to XBPM 9ID-BD-5 at 53.43 m (r10) and the CSSI station at 54.992 m (r8, ELOG 916) (listed directly after the CSSI station)
components.plain: A device that measures the shape of the X-ray wave itself, to check the mirrors and lenses are not distorting it.
components.expert: Compact X-ray wavefront sensor assembly (APS Optics group design by X. Shi, presented at the 2023 InterCAT TWG) for at-wavelength characterisation of the focused beam; sensing principle not stated in public pages.

components.name: High-load hexapod sample stage (GI-XPCS)
components.distanceNote: approx/derived: 'downstream of CSSI Solid Sample Station on the stationary granite of the GIXS table' (r40); manual gives hexapod centre to KB-H 1.552 m and to KB-V 1.818 m (r8) which, with KB-H ~0.65 m upstream of 54.992 m, puts it near 55.9 m
components.plain: A six-legged robotic platform that holds heavier sample cells steady for the 'twinkling speckle' measurements.
components.expert: Aerotech HEX500-350HL (500 mm diameter, high load), Automation1 iXR3/XSP3-10 drives; identical to the 8-ID-I rheometer hexapod; used by the Bluesky 'gixpcs' configuration with Grand Tube motion and EIGER 16M. Received 2024-10-07 (S/N 486416-01) (r40, ELOG 893).

components.name: GIXS diffractometer (from 8-ID-E) on granite translation
components.distanceNote: exact: 'GIXS: 56590' mm (r8, ELOG 916)
components.plain: A sturdy sample stage for flat-lying films, where films can be heated, cooled, exposed to solvent vapour or spin-coated while X-rays watch.
components.expert: Legacy 8-ID-E GISAXS/GIWAXS diffractometer and infrastructure for horizontal samples, on a translatable granite; environments: Linkam HFSX350-GI (-196/-180..350/300 C), solvent-vapour annealing (Nealey chamber), spin coating/deposition, user solar simulator; UR3e sample robot.

components.name: GIWAXS detector Pilatus 1M-F on motion system 9ID-BI-7
components.distanceNote: approx: in air immediately downstream/beside the GIXS sample; position variable on the WAXS detector motion system (r8)
components.plain: A camera close to the film that catches X-rays scattered at wide angles, revealing how molecules are packed.
components.expert: Dectris Pilatus 1M-F, 172 um pixels (standard Pilatus), 135 fps (directory), HDF5 via areaDetector; in-air WAXS detector positioning system 9ID-BI-7.

components.distanceNote: approx start: detector distances 2.9-21.8 m from the CSSI sample (r4) imply detector z ~57.9-76.8 m; tube length ~20.5 m (r20) -> ~57.4-77.9 m; FDR flight path 58.0-76.0 m (r1)

components.distanceNote: movable inside the Grand Tube (exact mounting not published)

geometryNotes: Single, non-canted ID line (dual-inline straight, only the downstream revolver installed; source point ~+1.25 m from the straight centre; all distances here are from the straight-section centre as in the FDR tables). Everything sits on the main experiment-hall floor (no LOM or long-beamline building): 9-ID-A FOE (~23.6-36.9 m, wedge-shaped in plan per FDR Fig. 4.51), shielded transport, the small 9-ID-MH mini-hutch (~41.5-45 m, as-built addition), shielded transport, the 9-ID-D station (~47-57.5 m) and the free-standing Grand Tube 9-ID-GT (~57.5-78 m) that is its own pink-beam-rated shielding: a light-grey 2.75 m-diameter cylinder of ~4 flanged sections with stiffener rings and a dished downstream head, resting on saddles on the floor, outside any hutch (APS photo, r4). The line ends close to the hall's outer wall (~90 m available). Optics: all upstream deflections are horizontal. MR-1 (flat) and MR-2 (bender) form a horizontal offset pair (~2.9 m apart in the layout). The HDCM deflects horizontally (mono beam ~10 mm outboard of the pink path at 42.4 m; masks PM-5 and XBPM have dual apertures/bypass). The surveyed XBPM bodies at 42.42 m and 53.40 m sit at almost the same horizontal offset from the white-beam axis (X = -8.79 / -8.64 mm), so the downstream beam runs parallel to the original axis, displaced sideways (r10). The KB pair (V then H) is the exception: the V mirror deflects the beam vertically (FDR 2.5 mrad grazing, i.e. ~5 mrad upward or downward, direction not documented) and the H mirror horizontally, focusing ~0.65 m downstream. Beam height ~1.4 m above floor throughout (FDR). Inside 9-ID-D (as-built isometric, r8): upstream optical table (fast shutter, attenuator) -> slits SL-4 -> CRL-2 transfocator stand -> slits SL-5 + XBPM-2 table -> KB UHV chamber on granite -> window -> round multi-port CSSI sample chamber on granite -> stationary granite with hexapod -> GIXS diffractometer on translating granite with in-air Pilatus WAXS detector arm -> Grand Tube entrance flange in the downstream wall. Two sample geometries: CSSI sample surface VERTICAL (incidence and specular reflection in the horizontal plane, so the reflected beam and exit-angle axis spread sideways in the tube); GIXS samples HORIZONTAL (classic GISAXS, exit angles vertical). Detector carriage translates along z and in x/y within the 2.75 m bore. Exact as-built z positions are public only for the CSSI station (54.992 m), GIXS (56.590 m) and the two XBPMs (42.38 m, 53.43 m); other positions are estimates (+/-1 m). Mirror-deflection sense (inboard vs outboard) of MR-1/MR-2 is not documented; only the mono-vs-pink offset direction is.

interactiveIdeas.title: Skip a stone with X-rays: the critical angle
interactiveIdeas.concept: A slider tilts a silicon wafer from 0 to 1 deg in front of an X-ray beam. Below the critical angle the beam reflects almost totally and only a few-nm-deep evanescent wave enters; above it the beam dives in. Show reflectivity curve, penetration depth and the footprint stretching across the wafer.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Why surface X-ray methods work at tiny angles, how depth sensitivity is tuned, and why a 1 um beam paints a ~0.2 mm stripe on the sample.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: alpha_c = sqrt(2 delta), delta proportional to lambda^2 rho_e: Si alpha_c ~0.20 deg (3.5 mrad) and Au ~0.50 deg at 8.8 keV, scaling as 1/E. Penetration depth below alpha_c ~ lambda/(4 pi sqrt(alpha_c^2 - alpha^2)) ~ a few nm (include beta for absorption). Footprint = beam size / sin(alpha): 0.75 um at 0.2 deg -> ~215 um. Yoneda peak at alpha_f = alpha_c.

interactiveIdeas.title: Speckle zoom: why the Grand Tube is 20 m long
interactiveIdeas.concept: Drag the EIGER/MM-PAD along the tube (2.9-21.8 m) and sideways; choose energy (6-25 keV) and focal spot (0.6-3.5 um). The speckle pattern rescales live over a pixel grid; meters show oversampling ratio and the finest resolvable feature.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: The core trade-off of coherent imaging: far away = speckles big enough to sample (oversampling), close or off-axis = higher q = finer detail; the tube allows both by moving the detector in 3D.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Speckle size s ~ lambda D / d (d = illuminated size projected normal to the exit direction); oversampling O = s/p >= 2 per dimension (Nyquist), ~5 preferred. Examples: 8.8 keV, D = 20 m, d = 0.75 um -> s ~3.8 mm (~50 EIGER pixels); 25 keV, d = 3.5 um, D = 20 m -> s ~0.28 mm (O ~1.9 with 150 um MM-PAD pixels). Half-period resolution ~ pi/q_max, q_max = (4 pi/lambda) sin(theta_max): detector half-width 0.155 m at 20 m and 8.8 keV gives ~9 nm; at 2.9 m ~1.3 nm. In grazing incidence resolution is anisotropic (poor along the beam footprint) - rotation series fix this.

interactiveIdeas.title: Lloyd's mirror in the hard X-ray world
interactiveIdeas.concept: A glowing point (a nanoscale feature) floats above a mirror-like substrate. Move it up and down and watch interference fringes appear on a virtual detector near the horizon, then reverse: given fringes, guess the height.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: How a substrate acts as a built-in reference beam, turning surface scattering into a hologram that encodes height from a single image.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Two paths: direct scattering and scattering reflected by the substrate (phase flip ~pi near alpha_f = 0 where Fresnel reflectance -> 1). Fringe period in qz ~ 2 pi/(2d) for height d; strongest for alpha_f < ~0.3 deg and alpha_i above alpha_c (Chu et al. 2023). Keep Fresnel reflectivity and absorption; it is dark-field (away from specular).

interactiveIdeas.title: Then and now: how orderly is the X-ray beam?
interactiveIdeas.concept: Two virtual pinholes (Young's double slit) at 30 m from the source: toggle between the 1996-2023 APS and APS-U sources and energies. Fringe visibility and the number of 'coherent modes' across the beam change dramatically, especially horizontally.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: What 'coherence' means and why the multi-bend-achromat upgrade made CSSI practical.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Transverse coherence length (rms) xi = lambda z/(2 pi Sigma), Sigma = sqrt(sigma_e^2 + sigma_r^2), sigma_r = sqrt(2 lambda L)/(4 pi). At 10 keV, 30 m: APS-U xi_x ~48 um (round mode), old APS ~2 um; vertical ~70 um vs ~58 um. Coherent fraction per plane = (lambda/4pi)/(Sigma Sigma'): ~2.6% (round) / ~6% (flat) total at 10 keV vs ~0.05% before. Use r15 parameters; do not use the 2019 FDR 'brightness mode' as current. r15 values are zero-current; the 9-ID source slide (r9) plots ~6% coherent fraction at 10 keV (~2% at 25 keV) for APS-U vs ~0.05% for the old APS, consistent with the flat-beam case. Show coherent FLUX (brilliance x (lambda/2)^2), not total flux, as the quantity that rose ~100x.

interactiveIdeas.title: Twinkle, twinkle: build a g2 curve
interactiveIdeas.concept: A live speckle movie from a thin polymer film; the user chooses temperature (viscosity) and film thickness. A cursor-picked speckle's intensity trace feeds a real-time correlation function g2(tau).
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: How XPCS turns flicker into a relaxation time and how different motions (diffusion, capillary waves) leave different q-dependences.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: g2(q,tau) = 1 + beta |f(q,tau)|^2, f = exp(-Gamma tau) for simple relaxation; diffusion Gamma = D q^2; overdamped capillary waves on thick films Gamma = gamma q/(2 eta) (thin films: Gamma ~ gamma h^3 q^4/(3 eta)); beta (speckle contrast) < 1 set by coherence and pixel/speckle ratio. Fastest time limited by detector (~2 ms at 400-550 fps) and by photons: SNR ~ beta * I * sqrt(T tau N); at fixed SNR the shortest tau scales as 1/brilliance^2. 9-ID window 1e-3-1e3 s.

interactiveIdeas.title: Zoom lens of beryllium: the transfocators
interactiveIdeas.concept: Toggle the 9 + 10 lens cassettes of CRL-1 and CRL-2 (binary stacks of R = 2000..100 um lenses) and the KB mirrors to zoom the spot from ~30 um to ~0.5 um at the sample; see flux and number of coherent modes accepted.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: How X-ray lenses work (weakly), why many lenses are stacked, and the trade-off between spot size and coherent flux.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Thin-lens focal length f = R/(2 N delta) for paraboloid lenses (Be delta ~4.4e-6 at 8.8 keV, so N=1, R=100 um gives f ~11 m), combine stacks with 1/f = sum; imaging 1/p + 1/q = 1/f; spot ~ source size x magnification convolved with diffraction ~lambda/(2 NA). Use as-built cassettes (r11), not the FDR 12-stack lists.

funFacts: The Grand Tube weighs about 100,000 lb (~45 t). It was unloaded at Argonne in four crated sections in August 2023, assembled in three weeks and installed at 9-ID in Sep-Oct 2023 (r21, r23, r41, r7).
It is big enough to walk inside: about 2.75 m (9 ft) across and ~20 m long; entering it requires a formal access procedure (r20, r4, r8).
Its 8 mm stainless-steel wall doubles as radiation shielding, so the tube itself is a certified X-ray enclosure (9-ID-GT) rather than a pipe inside a hutch (r20, r6).

The first CSSI demonstration (2012, APS 8-ID-E) used a CCD only 0.7 m from the sample that detected just ~0.13% of scattered photons. It needed a few hours to record one pattern, peaking at 3,000 counts, from a gold 'Argonne' test pattern 400 um long, 5 um wide and 40 nm thick (r3, r24).
The KB mirrors must hold their angle to 14-19 nanoradians, the angle a 1 cm coin subtends seen from about 500-700 km away (r16, r17; comparison derived).
At a 1 degree grazing angle, raising the sample by 1 um slides the beam footprint ~57 um along the surface; the stage must find the surface to <50 nm (r3).

In CSSI the mirror-like reflection can be as bright as the incoming beam while useful speckles are 8-10 orders of magnitude fainter - up to 1e11 counts/s per pixel near the critical angle - so a special mixed-mode detector (MM-PAD) replaces the usual beamstop (r3).
Before the upgrade the horizontal coherence length 30 m from the source was only ~2 um at 10 keV; at the upgraded APS it is ~40-50 um (derived from r15).
9-ID used to host the USAXS instrument (now at 12-ID-E) and the Bionanoprobe (now at 2-ID-D); its GIXS instrument moved in from 8-ID-E (r6, r19).
The holographic analysis echoes Humphrey Lloyd's 19th-century mirror-interference experiment, redone with hard X-rays and a silicon wafer as the mirror (r26).

openQuestions: As-built z positions are public only for the CSSI station (54.992 m), GIXS (56.590 m) and XBPMs (42.38 / 53.43 m); the '09-ID Beamline Component Reference Table' and optics schematic are on access-restricted Box. All other positions here are FDR values or +/-1 m estimates from isometric drawings.
Enclosure boundaries of 9-ID-MH (~41.5-45 m) and the 9-ID-D / Grand Tube interface (~57.5 m) are estimates; hutch widths are not published (FDR plan figure appears anisotropically scaled).

Mirror incidence angles as built are not published (FDR: single M1 at 2.4 mrad; shielding analysis assumed two mirrors at >=3.0 mrad). The fourth mirror stripe is unidentified, and whether MR-1 deflects inboard or outboard is unknown.

HDCM: crystal set (FDR Si(111) only; PDR Si(111)+Si(220); the directory lists a 'High resolution' mode with dE/E = 2.8e-5, which would fit Si(311)) and the fixed-exit offset (FDR '2 mm offset' vs ~10 mm pink/mono separation at 42.4 m in the XBPM drawing) are unconfirmed. No DMM appears in as-built lists although FDR/PDR reserved one.

CRL-1 moved from the FOE (FDR 32.4 m) to the mini-hutch (~43 m) and the lens sets changed (as-built 9/10 cassettes, all 2D, R >= 100 um vs FDR 12 stacks incl. 1D and R = 50 um), yet the Beamline Directory still quotes the FDR focal sizes (29 x 16 um, 3.5 x 1.7 um); actual as-built spot sizes and fluxes need confirmation.

Directory fluxes (e.g. 3.4e13 ph/s CRL-1, 9.4e12 CRL-2, 1.2e13 KB at 8.8 keV; 3.2e11 / 3.7e11 at 25 keV, and '3 um x 12 um' for CRL-2 high energy) are inconsistent with FDR Table 4.58 by roughly a bandwidth factor or 10x; treat as indicative.

KB working distance: FDR geometry (V 1.0 m / H 0.8 m upstream of sample), MEDSI 2020 (550 mm) and SPIE 2025 abstract ('about 650 mm', verified) differ; ~650 mm is the most recent. The full SPIE paper (measured stability; the abstract states a 55 nrad sample-stability requirement vs 50 nrad in 2020) was not accessible.

Grand Tube dimensions differ by source: 20 m x 2.75 m (Struct. Dyn. 2025), 20.5 m x 2.75 m (shielding paper), '66-foot, ~nine feet' (feature page), '70-foot' (APS news), '20 m x 3 m' (2023 update). The overall vessel incl. heads is probably ~21 m; inner bore assumed 2.75 m.

Detector specifics: EIGER 16M variant (EIGER2 X vs XE; 400/550 fps suggests XE) and the MM-PAD version, mounting and travel ranges inside the tube are not published; beamstop arrangement for GISAXS/CSSI is undocumented.
The FDR liquid-surface diffractometer (57 m, double-crystal beam tilter for liquid/liquid interfaces) is absent from as-built lists; status (deferred or cancelled) unknown.
Second undulator: the upstream slot is empty; no public schedule for installing the planned planar U21 (FDR flux tables assume both devices, 4.6 m).

Exact first-light date: the manual says only 'first light in 2024-2'. Whether CSSI (vs GIXS/GI-XPCS) is routinely offered to general users or mainly in partner/collaborative mode in 2026-3 is not stated beyond the 80% GUP allocation 'for GI-SAXS/WAXS/XPCS and CSSI'.
No published 9-ID (post-upgrade) CSSI reconstruction or GI-XPCS paper was found as of 2026-10-08; science cases cite pre-upgrade 8-ID/P10 work and the legacy 8-ID-E instrument.

'First light in 2024-2' (manual) predates the 9-ID-A shielding verification (2024-12-18), so it cannot mean X-rays in the hutches. The date the first X-rays reached 9-ID-A or 9-ID-D is not published; technical commissioning began the week of 2025-02-03.
The tag 9ID-BD-3 is used both for the mono flag inside the HDCM (9-ID-A) and for XBPM-1 in 9-ID-MH; ask staff which is correct before labelling hotspots.
Vertical-deflection sense of the KB-V mirror (beam up or down) and as-built KB angles and coating are not published.
